license.attribution: arXiv.org. Abstracts are authored text, offered by arXiv as descriptive metadata. Attributed here as a courtesy that CC0 does not require.
license.verified_by: Fetched and read https://info.arxiv.org/help/api/tou.html on 2026-08-21. It states: 'You are free to use descriptive metadata about arXiv e-prints under the terms of the Creative Commons Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Declaration.' Its footnote 1 defines the term: 'Descriptive metadata includes information for discovery and identification purposes, and includes fields such as title, abstract, authors, identifiers, and classification terms.' The abstract is therefore metadata, not e-print content. The same page's prohibition -- 'Store and serve arXiv e-prints (PDFs, source files, or other content) from your servers' -- was read and does not reach abstracts; no PDF or source file is fetched or stored.

note: Abstracts for records in enriched_alignment_research_events.json, which has no raw provenance in this repo. See pdoom-data#88.

license_correction.why: The first version of this block asserted 'arXiv API Terms of Use read 2026-08-21' when they had NOT been read, and carried reuse_basis 'facts_and_link_only' copied from the forum adapters, which is false here because this tool stores abstract text verbatim. A fabricated verification claim is the exact failure this repository exists to prevent. Corrected before first commit, so no history is rewritten; recorded rather than silently replaced.

transformations.what: runs of whitespace and newlines collapsed to single spaces
transformations.why: arXiv wraps the abstract for display; the wrapping is not content
the repository is ASCII-only and enforces it in CI
transformations.note: an accented letter survives as its base letter; a character with no ASCII decomposition is DELETED, which is why chars_dropped is recorded per record and shown to the reviewer before the choice

transformations.what: cut at the last sentence boundary at or before 600 characters
transformations.why: event_v1 allows 1000; 600 is an editorial choice, not a schema requirement, so it is named here as a choice
transformations.note: applied only when the abstract exceeds the limit; is_excerpt records it

audit_chain: <- this dump's data.jsonl, field 'abstract' (verbatim, unmodified) and 'abstract_ascii'

audit_chain_gap.gap: this dump does NOT record the versioned Atom entry the text was read from
audit_chain_gap.consequence: an abstract can differ between v1 and v3, so the chain reaches the paper but not the exact words retrieved
audit_chain_gap.fixed_from: the next dump onward; entry_id and arxiv_version are now recorded
audit_chain_gap.found: by checking the audit_chain claim against the file rather than against the intention, immediately after writing it
